Unconventional: No

Comments: On 8/10/23 at 1201 hrs., I conducted an incident inspection of Madtick Development Corp.'s Musser Associates 2 well site (API 063-32934) in East Mahoning Twp., Indiana Co. The inspection was conducted in response to a phone call received on 8/10/23 from the landowner, indicating that a production fluid release was observed at the well site. The landowner unsuccessfully attempted to contact the operator, and then reported the release to the Department. Upon inspection of the site, stressed/dead vegetation was observed around the production fluid tank onsite, and in an adjacent corn field. The area of dead vegetation appears to be approximately 30-45 feet wide and extends approximately 200-250 feet to the North of the well site. The release appears to be originating from a tank onsite. The tank appears to be empty. The release appears to be over 1 barrel of fluid. In addition to the release, it was observed that the well is equipped for production. A well tag is not affixed to the completed well. A site ID sign is posted, but is illegible and does not display the required information.Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), and 78.66(b) are being cited for failure by the operator to report the release, and are immediately being closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of OGA 3211(G) and OGA 3211(H) are cited for the lack of site ID sign and well tag. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1) are cited for the release of production fluids from the tank onto the ground. The violations will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release anddemonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8274508
Permit API: 015-23116
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2026
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's VanBlarcom (03-113) R well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 5/11/2026 at 1200 hours. The weather was 54 degrees F with mostly cloudy skies. An Act 9 sign remained in place at the site entrance.The VanBlarcom (03-113-01) R 1H well appeared capable of production. No bubbling was observed in the fluids held within the well cellar. Areas surrounding the well pad remained permanently stabilized with vegetative cover. No evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A stormwater basin remains in place for post-construction stormwater management (photo #2). Secondary containment structures appeared functional and displayed no evidence of leaking. On 4/15/2026, Repsol reported to the DEP that elevated electrical conductivity fluids were discovered on the pad surface in the area where vehicles travel. The DEP conducted an incident inspection on 4/15 (inspection record #4179711) to evaluate the report from Repsol. Repsol later provided analytical results of the fluids to the DEP and violations were cited on 4/24/2026 indicating a potential produced fluids release of an unknown quantity to the pad surface. During this inspection, the area of the discovered release was inspected. All fluids within the area were field measured for electrical conductivity and returned readings ranging from 210 to 240us/cm. Impacted solid materials recovered during the cleanup are stored onsite in a lined and covered container (photo #6). Violations cited against API #015-23116 on 4/24/2026 will remain outstanding until attainment with Act 2 standards are met. I departed the site at 1320 hours.

Comments: During a routine inspection (ID 3840906) on 9/30/24 puddles were observed on the pad surface. A violation of CSL 402(b) was originally cited in inspection 3840906.Due to the unknown volume of released fluid, it is again recommended that Chesapeake pursue remediation under Act 2 requirements.

Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Mr. Subra said that Tobias would be cleaning out the culverts later that day.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/10/2024
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8171036
Permit API: 081-21912
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/10/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 1/8/24. The operator reported that the release of produced fluid occurred in a path from the frac tank battery to the production tanks on the well pad when a driver who had already off-loaded produced fluid from the production tanks into the frac tanks left the valve open on the truck which allowed an estimated half barrel of residual produced fluid to leak onto the pad surface when he drove back to the production tanks. The site was covered with snow, slush, and puddles of stormwater during this inspection. I met with Kirby Steck of Range upon arriving on location. He showed me the path where a water truck driver released an estimated half barrel of produced fluid. I conducted screening of the fluid on the well pad between the production tanks and the frac tanks. Near the production tanks, in the offloading area, a puddle of fluid was present beneath a water truck that was emptying the production tanks. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid on the puddle was 5.99 mS/cm. Between the production tanks and the frac tanks, the EC readings were below 2 mS/cm. In a puddle near the frac tank battery, the EC was 2.30 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was also on location sucking up fluid from the pad surface. According to Mr. Steck, the plan was to continue sucking up fluid from the well pad that day and the following day, 1/11/24, and to have a crew come on 1/11/24 to begin excavation on the well pad. Mr. Steck said that the estimated volume of the release was changed to half a barrel after speaking with the trucking contractor who said that the truck had already off-loaded the fluid from the truck at the time that the release occurred. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up the fluid with elevated electrical conductivity on the pad and to excavate the impacted pad material. Violations noted. Violations remain outstanding for previous releases on the pad.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia's Crain well site located in Rome Township, Bradford County on 10/6/2023 at 1025 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Chesapeake. Complaint tracking system (CTS) ID # 375421 is tied to this release within CTS.Chesapeake reported that on 10/5/2023 at 1030 hours, a release of approximately 150 gallons of methanol was spilled to the pad surface when its storage container was being moved with a forklift. Chesapeake reported that a water truck was utilized to recover all of the standing fluid on the pad surface and the impacted area was excavated. All impacted pad material was placed in waste containers and covered. Chesapeake reported that no portion of the release was able to runoff the site. Chesapeake confirmed that the clean-up was completed on 10/5/2023 and had an environmental consultant respond to collect soil characterization samples. Comments: Arrived on location at 09:00 to conclude 72hr PBUTs. I was accompanied by Ken Kennedy (OGI supervisor) and Eric Rooney (Department Geologist). We met with Cabot O&GReps., Ben Whitaker and Keenan Small; Selman and Assoc. Reps., Brett Wambold and Miriah Palmatier. At ~ 09:25 ending pressures were checked using Cabots digital gauge. Annuli gas checks were performed starting at ~ 10:40. All pressures and gas checks were taken at the block and bleeds at the wells.-2H:(20x13): Pressure = 0.0psi., Gas = 100% LEL, 54% CH4 (*collected at 10:56)**(13x9): Pressure = 0.0psi., Gas = 100% LEL, 100% CH4 (*collected at 10:58)**(9x5): Pressure = 0.0psi.-4H:(20x13): Pressure = 0.0psi., Gas = 0% LEL, 0% CH4(13x9): Pressure = 0.0psi., Gas = 100% LEL, 50% CH4 (*collected at 10:54)**(9x5): Pressure = 22psi.-6H:(20x13): Pressure = 0.0psi., Gas = 100% LEL, 12% CH4 (*collected at 10:48)**(13x9): Pressure = 0.0psi., Gas = 100% LEL, 100% CH4 (*collected at 10:50)**(9x5): Pressure = 27psi.-8H:(20x13): Pressure = 0.0 psi., Gas = 100% LEL, 29% CH4 (*collected at 10:43)**(13x9): Pressure = 0.0 psi., Gas = 100% LEL, 50% CH4 (*collected at 10:45)**(9x5): Pressure = 246psi.- Following conclusion of area residents domestic well water sampling, all wells annuli were turned over for venting.** Although no pre-PBUT flows or post-PBUT pressures were detected at any of these wells (13x9) or (20x13) annuli, gas was detected, confirmed by Selman & Associates and samples were collected at end of PBUTs. Following the analysis of the collected annular gas samples, the Dept. requests that Cabot assess these conditions further and contact the Dept. with Cabot¿s assessment and a plan to perform a 3rd PBUT on these Howell wells.Left site at 11:05.

The area immediately downslope of the site to the access road appears to have been excavated at this time (Photos 4-5, 24-25).Tarp remains installed in the area from the site to the culvert inlet (Photos 9-13, 18-20), however it appears that the stockpile of excavated material from the pit has been removed.Tarps and BMPs remain installed and appear to be in the same condition as noted in IR 4021773 (Photos 6-8, 14-17).Glenn Wilson (Diversified) arrived on-site during the inspection. Wilson informed the Department of the following:- The tarp that was covering the slope immediately downslope of the site was moved to the North side of the site.- The stockpiled material from the pit was moved and placed on top of this tarp. - The slope immediately downslope of the site was excavated and also placed on the tarp.- All of this material is what is being removed from the site today. - No work has been done on the other side of the access road today, including probing for specific conductivity. - Operator plans to remove and replace the secondary containment on site.- Operator has a representative from the tank company on site today to assess if the tank will need to be replaced as well. - Site will be covered back up by tarp following today's material removal.Violations for the brine release remain outstanding.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-11-21
Comments: This site is located east off Pine City Road, south of the railroad grade and several hundred yards east of the storage yard. There was a several gallon oil release located at the tank battery for this well west of the storage yard. The oil spill is at the end of the tank discharge pipe on the outer embankment of the secondary containment. WQS Taylor contacted Ben Ochs about this oil release, he stated that he had spilled this oil about a week ago and was planning to clean it up. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using the Small Spill Cleanup Process, which states: For spills of less than 42 gallons at a well site that do not pollute waters of the Commonwealth or threaten pollution of these waters, the responsible party should remove the soil visibly impacted by the spill upon discovery of the spill and should dispose of the impacted soil by a method permitted by law. The responsible party should notify the Department of its intent to remediate a spill in this manner at the time notification of the spill is made.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/14/2021 to CATALYST ENERGY INC in Ceres Twp, McKean county. OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CATALYST ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/13/2021
Violation Code: OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
Violation ID: 917125
Permit API: 083-49649
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Ceres Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 5/14/2021
Comments: This well was drilled in 2004 and never completed. I could not find a well sign or well tag on this site. The well was on regulatory inactive status for 5 years from 2007 until 2012 when it expired. The well status was never changed and continued to be reported as inactive but the status has been changed to active now. No production has ever been reported for the well, it is not equipped for production and is by definition "Abandoned". The well is shut in, has no gauge on it and there are bubbles coming up from the annulus of the surface casing and the conductor. The well has 502' of 7" casing cemented back to surface. I counted anywhere from 60 to 80 bubbles a minute coming from the annulus. Catalyst took possession of the well from Enervest in 10/2019.
